h1: The 8 Best 2-Bay NAS for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best 2-Bay NAS for Home Offices: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best 2-bay NAS for home offices in 2026, from Synology and QNAP to UGREEN and Asustor, with picks for every budget.
summary: The Synology DS223 is the best overall for first time buyers thanks to the easiest software. The UGREEN DXP2800 suits photo and video work, the QNAP TS-264 comes with 8GB of RAM for apps, and the Asustor and UGREEN DH2300 are the budget choices. The Synology DS725+ is the growth pick.
intro: The mistake with a 2-bay NAS is thinking the box matters more than the drives. Every NAS here ships diskless, so the real price is the enclosure plus two hard drives, and RAID 1, which mirrors the drives, means you only get the capacity of one. Buy the drives with the same care as the box.

We reviewed eight 2-bay NAS units on paper, comparing software, networking, RAM, drive support and upgrade paths from the listings. Picks are ranked by fit for a home office that mostly backs up and shares files.

products.name: Synology DS223 Home & Office Backup Hub (2-Bay Diskless NAS)
products.verdict: The easiest NAS software for first time buyers.
products.description:
The DS223 is a 2 bay diskless NAS running Synology's DSM operating system with RAID 1 support. It is a Value series model with soldered RAM, so memory cannot be upgraded, and it focuses on backup and basic surveillance monitoring.

It ranks first because DSM is the easiest NAS software to learn, which counts for more than raw power in a small office. The tradeoff is hardware: the QNAP and TERRAMASTER offer more RAM or CPU at similar money.

Buy it if you want to set up backups and shared folders with minimal fuss. Skip it if you plan to run many apps.
products.skipIf: You want to run many apps.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DXP2800 2-Bay
products.verdict: More processing headroom for photo and video work.
products.description:
The DXP2800 is a diskless 2 bay NAS running UGREEN NAS OS with RAID 1 support, built with content creator hardware in mind.

It ranks second because its extra headroom helps with photo and video libraries, but UGREEN's software is newer than DSM, so the polish trails Synology. The listing offers fewer spec numbers than some rivals.

Choose it if you handle large media files. Drives are sold separately.
products.skipIf: You want the most polished software.

products.name: QNAP TS-264-8G-US 2 Bay Desktop NAS
products.verdict: 8GB of RAM out of the box for running apps.
products.description:
The TS-264 is a 2 bay desktop NAS with 8GB RAM included, QTS software, and multi app and container support. It is diskless.

It ranks third because the included RAM saves an upgrade, but QTS has a steeper learning curve than DSM.

Pick it if you will run several apps or media servers at once.

products.name: TERRAMASTER F2-425 2-Bay NAS (Intel x86 Quad-Core)
products.verdict: Quad core Intel power with 2.5GbE and 4GB RAM.
products.description:
The F2-425 pairs an Intel x86 quad core CPU with 4GB RAM, 2.5GbE LAN and the TOS operating system in a 2 bay diskless chassis.

It ranks fourth because raw power is strong, yet TOS software is less polished than DSM.

Buy it if performance matters more than software finish.

products.name: QNAP TS-216G-US 2-Bay 2.5GbE Desktop NAS
products.verdict: Faster networking if your switch supports it.
products.description:
The TS-216G is a 2 bay desktop NAS with 2.5GbE networking, QTS and RAID 1 support, diskless.

It ranks below the TS-264 because the listing gives no RAM figure, so app headroom is unclear.

Pick it if you already have a 2.5GbE switch. Without one, the faster port goes unused.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DH2300 2-Bay Desktop NAS (Diskless)
products.verdict: Supports up to 64TB total capacity at a low price.
products.description:
The DH2300 is a 2 bay desktop NAS with UGREEN NAS OS and RAID 1 support, supporting up to 64TB total capacity, in the $100 to $200 tier.

It ranks sixth because it is a lower cost model than the DXP2800 and lists less hardware detail.

Choose it if you want room for large drives later without changing the enclosure.

products.name: Asustor Drivestor 2 Gen 2 (AS1202T) 2-Bay NAS
products.verdict: A budget NAS with 2.5GbE and a quad core CPU.
products.description:
The Drivestor 2 Gen 2 has a quad core 1.7GHz CPU, 2.5GbE networking, 1GB of soldered DDR4 RAM and 4K media server support in a 2 bay diskless chassis, in the $100 to $200 tier.

It ranks seventh because 1GB of RAM is thin for apps. It is aimed at plain backup and file sharing.

Buy it if budget is tight and needs are simple.

products.name: Synology DS725+ Expandable NAS (2-Bay Diskless)
products.verdict: Upgradeable RAM and expansion room, at the top price tier.
products.description:
The DS725+ is a Plus series 2 bay diskless NAS with upgradeable DDR4 RAM, expansion via Synology expansion units and DSM software, aimed at private cloud and small business use.

It ranks last only because of price, in the $500 and up tier, which most home offices do not need. It is the only pick here that grows with you.

Choose it for a business that will outgrow two bays.

whatMatters.detail: RAID 1 writes the same data to both drives, so one can fail without loss. You only get the capacity of one drive. It is not a backup, because deletions mirror too. Check for RAID 1 support in the title or specs.
Diskless means no drives included. You must buy two NAS rated drives. Budget for this on top of the box. Look for the word diskless in the title.
RAM affects apps and containers. Some units solder RAM so it cannot be upgraded. The QNAP TS-264 includes 8GB. Check the RAM line before buying.
2.5GbE is faster than gigabit but needs a 2.5GbE switch to benefit. Without one, it runs at gigabit. Check the LAN spec.
DSM, QTS, TOS and UGREEN NAS OS differ in polish. Synology's is easiest. Read the OS name on the listing.

cards.text: Synology DS223 offers DSM and RAID 1 with a backup focus.

cards.text: You expect to grow. Synology DS725+ has upgradeable RAM and expansion.

cards.text: You only need backup. Asustor Drivestor 2 Gen 2 and UGREEN DH2300 sit in the $100 to $200 tier.

faq.a: No, all are diskless. Buy two NAS rated drives separately.
Treating RAID 1 as a backup. It mirrors deletions, so keep a second copy elsewhere.

faq.q: Is the Plus series worth it over the DS223?
faq.a: Only if you need upgradeable RAM and expansion. The DS725+ costs far more.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Install the drives, power on and follow the setup wizard in the browser.

faq.q: How do I maintain a NAS?
faq.a: Keep firmware updated and check drive health regularly.

faq.q: Can I run a media server?
faq.a: The Asustor lists 4K media server support, and QNAP TS-264 suits Plex style apps.

finalTake: The Synology DS223 is the safest first NAS, and the UGREEN DXP2800 suits creators. Choose the QNAP TS-264 for apps, the Asustor for a tight budget and the DS725+ if you will grow. Budget for the drives too.
